children: Luxury-fashion company Brunello Cucinelli again lifted its sales expectations for the full year on the back of continued momentum, contrasting with lackluster performance elsewhere in Europe's luxury-goods sector.

The Italian group, known for its cashmere garments, said Thursday that it now expects sales for the year to rise by 12% at constant exchange rates from the 1.41 billion euros ($1.57 billion) it booked last year. Cucinelli had previously guided for 10%-11% growth, guidance that was itself expanded from an initial target of 10%. Sales next year should grow by around 10%, the company said.
"We believe that the brand's image around the world reflects what we have always aspired to: a belief in absolute luxury," the company's eponymous founder and executive chairman said.

The rosier view comes after the company netted sales of 374.2 million euros for the year's third quarter, up 13.5% from a year earlier, and picking up a little pace from the first six months. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha had forecast revenue of 371.2 million euros for the quarter. The larger retail channel led the charge, booking 17% growth in the quarter, while wholesale grew at a slower pace, Cucinelli said. New store openings, expansions and relocations have helped boost the company's direct retail sales across its 142 boutiques this year, it said.

Cucinelli's high-end positioning has left it almost alone, alongside storied Parisian fashion house Chanel, as a brand untarnished by the derailing of luxury's supercycle, analysts at Berenberg wrote in a recent note. The group's products are aimed squarely at the wealthier type of luxury consumer. Brands that target a broader and more aspirational public, such as Kering's Gucci or LVMH flagship brand Louis Vuitton, have taken a harder hit from inflation and other macro pressures that have dampened less affluent shoppers' ability to splash out. LVMH said earlier this week its mainstay fashion division, home to LV and Dior, lost 5% in sales compared with a year earlier in the third quarter.
"Brunello Cucinelli [has] consistent growth and near universal appeal," Berenberg said.
